title: nrminor/silly-fast-bfx pipeline parameters
description: Rapid metagenomic screening across named tool-specific reference specifications.

results.description: Root directory for the results bundle.

work_dir.description: Nextflow work directory. Defaults to NXF_WORK when set, otherwise work/ in the launch directory.

bqtools.description: Run-wide settings for BQTools CBQ read encodings.

block_size.description: CBQ virtual block size: a positive integer in bytes, optionally suffixed with K, M, or G (powers of 1024). Concatenation inherits this size from the encoded inputs.

skip_mapping.description: Default false. True suppresses the entire mapping branch without removing its reference specifications or disabling independently configured Sylph profiling.

deacon.description: Named Deacon reference specifications used to produce filtered read sets.

sylph.description: Named Sylph reference specifications used to sketch and profile selected read sets.

skope.description: Named Skope reference specifications used to query selected read sets.

mapping.description: Optional named mapping reference specifications; empty means no mapping. Each uses one explicit FASTA and one selection-profile source, not a union of profiles or FASTA files.

monoimage.description: Container image used by every pipeline process.

show_hidden.description: Display hidden parameters in the help message.

validate_params.description: Validate parameters against the pipeline schema.

reference_id.description: Identifier unique within one tool's reference specifications; used in results paths and read-set selections.

input.description: Search the input read set with this reference specification.

deacon_filtered.description: Deacon reference IDs whose filtered read sets are searched with this reference specification.

sha256.description: Optional expected SHA-256 digest; the pipeline verifies it and always records the observed digest.

kind.description: Read the artifact from a local filesystem path.

path.description: Absolute path to an existing local reference artifact or source file.

sha256.description: Optional expected SHA-256 digest for this local artifact.

kind.description: Download the artifact from an HTTPS URL.

url.description: HTTPS URL of the reference artifact or source file.

sha256.description: Optional expected SHA-256 digest for the downloaded artifact.

kmer_length.description: K-mer length for a source-built Deacon minimizer index; k plus window size minus one must be at most 96 and odd.

window_size.description: Minimizer window size for a source-built Deacon index; larger windows select fewer minimizers.

abs_threshold.description: Minimum absolute number of index minimizer hits required for a sequence record to match.

rel_threshold.description: Minimum proportion of a sequence record's minimizers that must hit the index, from 0 to 1.

prefix_length.description: Number of leading nucleotides searched in each sequence record; zero searches the entire record.

complexity_threshold.description: Ignore minimizers below this kdust complexity score from 0 to 1; null leaves complexity filtering disabled.

deplete.description: When false, retain matching records; when true, discard matching records and retain the complement.

id.description: Deacon reference ID attached to its filtered read sets and results.

fasta.description: FASTA or FASTQ source from which the pipeline builds a Deacon minimizer index.

index.description: Prebuilt Deacon minimizer index; mutually exclusive with fasta and build.

build.description: Index-construction settings used only when fasta is supplied.

filter.description: Settings that decide which input sequence records enter this Deacon-filtered read set.

references.description: Deacon reference specifications; an empty list creates no Deacon work.

kmer_length.description: K-mer length encoded in a source-built Sylph database; sample sketches queried against it must use the same value.

compression.description: Sylph database subsampling rate; smaller values retain more k-mers and increase database size and work.

individual_records.description: Treat each FASTA record as a separate reference genome instead of combining records by input file.

min_spacing.description: Minimum spacing between selected k-mers on reference genomes; this setting does not apply to sample read sketches.

kmer_length.description: K-mer length for sample read sketches; it must match the queried Sylph database and is derived from a source-built database when omitted.

compression.description: Sample-sketch subsampling rate; smaller values retain more k-mers and increase sensitivity, sketch size, and work. It cannot exceed the database rate and is derived from a source-built database when omitted.

no_dedup.description: Disable read deduplication while sketching to reduce memory use; Sylph does not recommend this for Illumina reads.

minimum_ani.description: Minimum adjusted average nucleotide identity percentage reported by Sylph profile; values below 95 can be inaccurate.

min_count_correct.description: Minimum k-mer multiplicity used for coverage correction; higher values favor precision over sensitivity.

min_number_kmers.description: Exclude reference genomes represented by fewer than this many sampled k-mers.

estimate_unknown.description: Estimate true coverage and scale sequence abundance by the estimated unknown-sequence percentage; this changes the Eff_cov column to True_cov.

estimate_read_counts.description: Very roughly estimate read counts in the Sequence_abundance column instead of relative abundance; enabling this also enables unknown-sequence estimation and may have caveats for long reads and complex environments.

read_seq_id.description: Read sequence identity percentage used only for unknown-sequence estimation; null lets Sylph detect it automatically.

metadata.description: One or more explicit sylph-tax metadata mappings applied to meaningful profiles from this reference specification.

id.description: Sylph reference ID used in process tags and results paths.

fastas.description: Ordered FASTA sources from which the pipeline builds one Sylph database.

database.description: Prebuilt Sylph .syldb database; mutually exclusive with fastas and build.

read_sets.description: Input and exact Deacon-filtered read sets profiled against this Sylph database.

build.description: Database-construction settings used only when fastas are supplied.

sample_sketch.description: Settings used to sketch each selected read set before profiling.

profile.description: Settings applied when profiling selected sample sketches against this database.

taxonomy.description: Optional explicit metadata mappings for producing taxonomy summaries in addition to raw profiles.

references.description: Sylph reference specifications; an empty list creates no Sylph work.

kmer_length.description: K-mer length for the Skope query index; it must be greater than the S-mer length unless all_kmers is enabled.

smer_length.description: Odd S-mer length used for open-syncmer selection; it must be smaller than the K-mer length. Ignored when all_kmers is enabled.

all_kmers.description: Bypass syncmer selection and consider every canonical target k-mer. Fraction sampling still applies; individual independently controls target grouping.

fraction.description: Fraction of selected target k-mers retained in a source-built query index; use one to retain all evidence after syncmer or all-kmer selection.

individual.description: Treat each target FASTA record separately instead of merging all records into one target.

fraction.description: Fraction of selected target k-mers considered during query, from greater than zero through one; prebuilt query indexes use their embedded fraction instead.

abundance_thresholds.description: Additional k-mer-abundance thresholds for containment estimates; each value adds threshold-specific output columns.

discriminatory.description: Consider only selected k-mers unique to each target when estimating containment.

confidence.description: Report confidence intervals, ANI estimates, and patchiness; the pipeline stores positions in source-built indexes when enabled, while prebuilt indexes must already contain positions.

limit.description: Approximate number of sample bases processed before stopping, such as 50M or 10G; null reads the complete read set.

id.description: Skope reference ID used in process tags and results paths.

targets.description: One target FASTA or FASTQ source, or an ordered nonempty list of target sources from which the pipeline builds a Skope query index. A list produces one target per source file.

query_index.description: Prebuilt Skope query index; mutually exclusive with targets and build.

read_sets.description: Input and exact Deacon-filtered read sets queried against this Skope index.

build.description: Query-index construction settings used only when targets are supplied.

query.description: Settings applied when querying each selected read set against this index.

references.description: Skope reference specifications; an empty list creates no Skope work.

mapping_profile_read_set.description: Singular selection: exactly one of input or one named Deacon-filtered read set. This supplies target-selection evidence, not necessarily the reads to map.

input.description: Select the input-read Sylph profile; this choice must be true, not a false placeholder selecting nothing.

deacon_filtered.description: One exact Deacon reference ID, not a list; selects the corresponding filtered-read Sylph profile.

input.description: True selects the input-read Sylph profile.

mapping_profile.description: One existing Sylph profile source per sample.

reference.description: Exact existing Sylph reference-specification ID, not a filename; select that specification's profile for the same sample and chosen profiling read set.

read_set.description: Singular selection of the Sylph profile read set used as target-selection evidence.

mapping_bound.description: Inclusive numeric bounds; null or omission disables each bound.

min.description: Inclusive lower bound; null or omission disables it. Missing row values fail an active bound, and a minimum above maximum is rejected.

max.description: Inclusive upper bound; null or omission disables it. Missing row values fail an active bound, and a minimum above maximum is rejected.

mapping_select.description: Optional filters on Sylph profile rows before FASTA subsetting; inclusive active bounds combine with AND, and no active bounds retain all rows.

sequence_abundance.description: Sylph's reported Sequence_abundance in percentage points, not a fraction or mapped-read count; preserve its interpretation as an estimate.

adjusted_ani.description: Sylph's reported Adjusted_ANI in percentage points, not a mapper identity threshold.

preset.description: Minimap2 preset for this platform; later mapping keeps records independent rather than paired fragments.

max_secondary.description: Maximum reported secondary alignments per read, not a count of primary or supplementary records and not an exhaustive search guarantee.

secondary_score_ratio.description: Minimap2 secondary-to-primary chain-score ratio, not identity, abundance, or MAPQ; mapper heuristics and count caps can still limit alternatives.

mapping_align.description: Competitive minimap2 mapping settings. Primary, secondary, supplementary, and unmapped records are retained in the BAM.

preset.description: Default map-ont; lr:hq is an explicit high-accuracy ONT option, never inferred from platform alone.

max_secondary.description: Default maximum of five reported secondary alignments per read.

preset.description: The sr preset; records are mapped independently, not as paired fragments, even when mate identity is retained.

max_secondary.description: Default maximum of 20 reported secondary alignments per read.

mapping_pileups.description: Alignoth pileup publication settings; these control visualization only, never BAM evidence, coverage, counts, or future classified-read tables.

enabled.description: Default true; publish Alignoth HTML for selected references with mapped support. This never changes alignment production or quantitative coverage and counts.

max_read_depth.description: Default 500; Alignoth display row cap only. Never apply it to BAM evidence, coverage, counts, or future classified-read tables.

mapping_read_store.description: Classified-read Parquet publication settings. The table is produced after BAM alignment for rapid exact-reference sequence retrieval, not as a mapper input or archival read store.

enabled.description: Default true; publish one self-contained classified-read Parquet table with one row per reported alignment and repeated original read payload. Unaligned sequences are omitted, but their counts remain available.

reference_allowlist.description: Optional text artifact of exact full reference names. Any matching placement includes the read with all its competitive placements; it has no effect on BAMs, mapping, coverage, or denominators.

id.description: Distinguishes mapping outputs and configurations; not an organism name, taxid, or Sylph target identifier.

profile.description: The exact one-reference, one-read-set Sylph profile source used for selection.

fasta.description: One local or HTTPS candidate FASTA following existing source conventions. It is explicit, never implicitly taken from Sylph; retained Contig_name values match complete record headers exactly.

select.description: Inclusive Sylph profile filters applied before exact-header FASTA subsetting.

read_sets.description: Mapping input choices, independent of the profiling read set. Input and/or named filtered sets are allowed; each later produces separate outputs with its own denominator.

align.description: Competitive minimap2 alignment settings for independently mapped read records.

pileups.description: Per-reference Alignoth pileup publication settings. Display limits never affect quantitative mapping evidence.

read_store.description: Post-alignment classified-read Parquet publication settings for rapid exact-reference sequence retrieval.

references.description: Optional named mapping reference specifications; an empty list creates no mapping work.
